label: Person
name: Adaldag
summary:
Adaldag (died 988) was Archbishop of Hamburg-Bremen from 937 to 988, one of the longest archiepiscopates in the see's history and the period during which Hamburg-Bremen became the dominant missionary centre for the Scandinavian north. His half-century of leadership coincided exactly with the Ottonian dynasty's consolidation of power in the German kingdom and its ambitious programme of northward ecclesiastical expansion.

Adaldag was a protégé of King Henry I and served continuously under Otto I (the Great), Otto II, and into the early reign of Otto III, becoming one of the few men who personally bridged the entire arc of Ottonian imperial achievement. Otto I trusted him as one of his most reliable ecclesiastical allies, and Adaldag participated in the key imperial assemblies and diplomatic missions of the Ottonian era.

His most significant ecclesiastical achievement was the establishment of the Danish bishoprics under Hamburg-Bremen's metropolitan authority. In 948 he consecrated three bishops for the Danish territories — at Schleswig, Ribe, and Aarhus — with King Harald Bluetooth's cooperation, representing a major milestone in Scandinavian Christianisation. These foundations eventually led to the full Christianisation of Denmark under Harald Bluetooth (c. 960) and were crucial to the development of Scandinavian Christianity.
